content.title: About
content.content: A hamburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a medium beef patty (1702 g), a bun, lettuce, a tomato slice, cheese, pickles and sauce. It is quick to prepare and often served with fries and a drink.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hamburger was served in the United States in the late 19th century.
There are more than 300 variations of toppings and sauces, from classic to exotic.
In Japan, rice‑bread buns are sometimes used instead of wheat buns.
The world’s largest hamburger weighed over 1 ton and was made in the USA in 2012.
In some countries the hamburger is considered a national dish.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: A medium patty (≈ 100 g) provides about 20 g of protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hamburgers supply vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The high calorie content offers a quick source of energy for active lifestyles.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc from beef supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: High calories and saturated fat
items.content: One hamburger can contain 500‑800 kcal and a notable amount of saturated fat, which may be undesirable for weight management.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sauces and processed buns often contain high levels of salt, potentially raising blood pressure.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Buns may contain gluten and dairy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Nitrites in processed meat
items.content: Some pre‑made patties contain nitrites that can form potentially harmful compounds when cooked at high temperatures.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hamburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding the bottom bun. You can add extra vegetables, swap the sauce, or choose a whole‑grain bun for a healthier option.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked patties in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, and keep buns in a dry place for several days. Frozen patties retain quality for up to 3 months.
